variables.name: DATABASE_URL
variables.description: Async connection string assembled from the POSTGRES_* inputs. Not settable from the environment; ENV_VARS.md documented it as a required input, which was drift.

variables.name: REDIS_URL
variables.description: Assembled from REDIS_HOST, REDIS_PORT, REDIS_DB, and REDIS_PASSWORD.

variables.name: EMBEDDING_DIMENSION
variables.description: One of the five points of the embedding dimension contract; see ADR-002.

variables.name: TIMEZONE
variables.description: The field's own comment requires an IANA zone name, and EDT is not one. Tracked as the timezone-not-iana finding; the fix is an application change.

variables.name: REDIS_PASSWORD
variables.required: in the production stack; deliberately empty on the internal network in base and dev

variables.name: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
variables.description: A live value was committed and pushed before governance adoption; rotation is required. See the secrets-pushed-to-remote finding.

variables.name: LOGFIRE_TOKEN
variables.description: Telemetry is sent only when this is present, which is what makes the scrubbed-subprocess extraction safe. A live value was committed and pushed; rotation is required.

variables.name: GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_MCP_CLIENT_ID
variables.removal_milestone: Remove once no deployment sets it and the direct Google REST executor is the only path

variables.name: GOOGLE_DRIVE_CLIENT_ID
variables.removal_milestone: Remove once no deployment sets it

variables.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
variables.description: Present in the template under the embeddings section but absent from Settings, so extra="ignore" drops it silently. Either the embeddings client should read it or it should be removed.

variables.name: ENABLE_CODE_EXECUTION
variables.description: Present in the template but absent from Settings. Code execution is gated by the generator context flag, not by this variable.

variables.name: CODE_EXECUTION_MAX_ALLOCATIONS
variables.description: Settings has CODE_EXECUTION_MAX_MEMORY_MB instead; this looks like a rename that left the template behind.

variables.name: DOMAIN
variables.required: in the production stack, where Compose fails fast without it

variables.name: TRAEFIK_HTTP_PORT
variables.description: Configurable because this host already runs IIS on port 80.

variables.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL
variables.description: Baked into the image at build time. Restarting the container will not pick up a new value.

variables.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL
variables.description: Used by the chat WebSocket, the one direct browser-to-backend edge.

variables.name: BACKEND_URL
variables.description: Server-side only: the proxy route handlers use it. Never exposed to the browser, which is the point of the proxy layer. Note the default port differs from the constants module's 8100 default.

findings.detail: Seven keys appeared twice in backend/.env.example with identical values. Removed during Phase 0; the duplicate-key parse rule added in Phase 3 raises a finding rather than silently last-wins parsing.

ENV_VARS.md documents GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, S3_ENDPOINT_URL, DB_POOL_SIZE, and REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES, none of which exist, and lists the computed DATABASE_URL as a required input.
OPENAI_API_KEY, ENABLE_CODE_EXECUTION, and CODE_EXECUTION_MAX_ALLOCATIONS appear in backend/.env.example but have no reader in Settings, so extra="ignore" drops them silently.

The proxy layer defaults BACKEND_URL to port 8000 while the frontend constants module defaults to 8100. Both are fallbacks that only apply when the variable is unset, so a misconfigured deployment fails in two different ways depending on which module is asked.
